newsitem.title: USA: Chinese exec met U.S. official through donor -Post.
newsitem.headline: Chinese exec met U.S. official through donor -Post.

text.p: The head of China's state-run petrochemical company secured a private meeting with U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary through a Democratic Party donor described by White House aides as a "hustler," the New York Post reported on Friday.
Chinese executive Sheng Huaren, who according to the newspaper was trying to expand the chemical company's business in the United States, had a 15-minute meeting with O'Leary in October 1995.
The newspaper also quoted an Energy Department official as saying Sheng was a "previous acquaintance" who first met O'Leary in China in February 1995.
The New York Post said records showed that consultant Johnny Chung, who reportedly gave $366,000 to the Democratic National Committee (DNC), arranged the meeting through the DNC.
It said that he also arranged meetings between President Bill Clinton and other Chinese business associates.
The newspaper said it obtained its information from official records after filing a Freedom of Information Act request.

Republicans and at least one Democrat troubled by the possibility of foreign involvement in Democratic Party fund-raising, have called on U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno to appoint an independent counsel to investigate the DNC's fund-raising during last year's election campaign.

The New York post said that 6 months before O'Leary's meeting with the Beijing executive, National Security Council official Robert Suettinger wrote an electronic mail message that cast Chung in unflattering terms.

Suettinger said Chung "should be treated with a pinch of suspicion" and "my impression is that (Chung) is a hustler" who intends to "continue to make efforts to bring 'friends' into contact with the (president and first lady) -- to show one and all that he is a big shot, thereby enhancing his business."
The newspaper also quoted a letter written to O'Leary and bearing then DNC chief Don Fowler's signature that mentioned Chung's support for the party in asking for the Sheng meeting.

"Mr. Chung, one of the top supporters of the Democratic National Committee, has asked me to assist him with this request. I would appreciate your strong consideration to this invitation," the newspaper quoted the letter as saying.
Two days later, O'Leary met Sheng, the Post reported.
